title: Privacy & Pricing Clearance — Onboarding Handoff

Agreement to circulate a redline-friendly MSA starter, security pack, and updated pricing spreadsheet; schedule legal-to-legal next week.

Pricing model: monthly vs annual, committed throughput

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-06
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Platform: Zoom
Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Greenfield - Procurement), Liam O'Neal (Greenfield - Security), Priya Singh (Greenfield - Legal), Diego Ramos (Finance)
Shared links: Security pack: https://redwood.app/security/greenfield-pack.pdf, Pricing: https://redwood.app/sales/pricing/gb-quote-2025.xlsx

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete): goover of MSA/DPA, sla credits, byok options, pricing paths and data residency

00:00 Jordan Mills: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. Jordan from Redwood on the line with Ravi, our solutions eng. we're hoping to run through the procurement and legal asks so you have what you need to push to finish.
00:14 Maya Chen: Thanks Jordan. Quick note, we've got four people here, I'll just call out roles — Priya from legal, Liam for security, Diego for finance. We're punched for time so would like to get to the must-haves.
00:30 Jordan Mills: Totally. I'll start with the commercial bits and Ravi will tag in on the private deployment / KMS details. High level, we discussed previously hosted vs private — I know your preference is Private with BYOK for PHI-ish workloads, is that still right?
00:48 Liam O'Neal: Yeah, we need BYOK or customer-managed keys, plus audit logs retained for 13 months. Also, local residency for a subset of datasets — they must stay in our VPC in us-east-1.
01:05 Ravi Patel: Yep that maps. For Redwood Privet — sorry, Redwood Privet — Private deployment, we support customer KMS via external KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM for on-prem. KV cache is local to the cluster and keys never leave keystore unless you opt-in to export.
01:32 Priya Singh: A couple legal flags: we want explicit deletion commitments in the DPA — deletion of ephemeral data within 30 days and confirmation of deletion on termination, plus a clear subprocessor list and notice period for changes. Also termination assistance and escrow for model weights — we need clarity there.
01:50 Jordan Mills: Understood. On deletion we can commit to ephemeral request logs removal within 30 days; for audit logs we usually offer 13 months by default but can extend on request. Subprocessors we'll provide the current list and a process for notice. On escrow, that's an ask we see often — our standard is to discuss at enterprise contracting stage, may be a separate addendum.
02:18 Diego Ramos: On pricing — finance is trying to decide between committed throughput monthly vs pay-as-you-go. If we go committed, what's the flexibility and SLA credits if uptime dips?
02:34 Jordan Mills: Good q. Committed gives a discount tier based on provisioned GPU-hours and burst allowance. SLA credits are pro rata. Standard SLA is 99.9% across Dedicated/Private control plane with crediting structure in the MSA, but for enterprise we can negotiate higher SLOs or different credit formulas.
02:57 Maya Chen: Can you spell out the SLA credit calc? Last time I saw a table but it was hard to map to our bill.
03:10 Jordan Mills: Sure, brief version: if monthly uptime < SLA threshold, we credit a percentage of monthly fees: e.g., 99.9–99.0 = 10% credit, 99.0–95.0 = 25%, <95 = 50% — that's illustrative; we'll include the exact table in the MSA.
03:33 Priya Singh: We typically need a shorter termination notice and exit assistance — 60 days minimum for tooling/data extraction. Also, we want clarity on data egress fees on termination.
03:49 Jordan Mills: We can propose a 60-day data extraction assistance window; egress fees are usually per GB for hosted cases, but for private deployments generally zero egress inside the customer's VPC, outside transfers could be charged. We'll document that nuance.
04:12 Liam O'Neal: Security: SOC2 type II report, pen test recency, and a rights-to-audit clause. Also, do you roster subprocessors in the MSA or DPA?
04:27 Ravi Patel: Security pack has SOC2 attestation and last pen test summary (Q2 2025). We generally list subprocessors in the DPA and provide notification windows; if you need explicit approval for certain subprocessor categories we can discuss.
04:45 Priya Singh: On data residency: we will need contractual confirmation that specified data sets remain in us-east-1 and not mirrored. How does Redwood handle fallback failover (multi-region) without copying our datasets?
04:59 Ravi Patel: Smart routing can route by policy; for private we can pin clusters to a region and use cross-region fallback only if configured. We'll note that any cross-region replication must be explicit and consented. There might be config flags in the private control plane.
05:20 Diego Ramos: Regarding discounts, is there an annual commit discount curve we can see? Also are there buyer protections if usage drops?
05:30 Jordan Mills: Yes, annual commits have step discounts. If usage drops below committed, we typically bill committed baseline but we can add flex allowances in the contract for startup-years. We'll show a few scenarios in the pricing spreadsheet.
05:46 Maya Chen: Ok, here's our priority list: DPA deletions/subprocessors, SLA credits & termination assistance, BYOK/KMS proof, and clear pricing scenarios. If we get those, procurement can push to legal signoff.
06:02 Jordan Mills: Perfect, we'll prioritize those. Ravi, can you outline how BYOK works in the private flow?
06:11 Ravi Patel: Sure. For Private we offer two patterns: 1) VPC with customer KMS where keys are managed in the customer's cloud account and Redwood's agents request unwrap operations, logs show key usage but keys never handled by Redwood; 2) On-prem HSM where we deploy agents behind your firewall and use an HSM for signing and encryption. In both, we can support key rotation and we surface KMS audit events to your SIEM.
06:36 Liam O'Neal: How does that affect backups and KV cache? If keys rotate, do you re-encrypt caches? We need a migration story.
06:47 Ravi Patel: Good question — caches are encrypted at rest with the active key. On rotation we re-encrypt lazily or during maintenance windows; we can add a forced re-encrypt path if required. We'll put the sequence in the deployment checklist.
07:05 Priya Singh: On legal language: we typically require a 30-day cure period for IP claims and liquidated damages caps. Do you accept liability caps tied to fees?
07:18 Jordan Mills: Our standard MSA has liability capped to a multiple of fees paid in the prior 12 months, with carveouts for gross negligence. We can take Priya's redlines and surface which clauses we can move on.
07:33 Priya Singh: Also open to negotiating a mutual NDA addendum for certain R&D inputs.
07:40 Jordan Mills: Sounds fair. We'll flag that as well.
07:45 Maya Chen: A few operational asks: can you provide a sample runbook for onboarding, and a timeline estimate for spinning up a private cluster (including KMS integration)?
07:55 Ravi Patel: Typical timeline: 4–6 weeks for a private cluster with standard infra if we have network access, keys, and a config review. Onboarding runbook and a checklist will be attached to the security pack.
08:12 Diego Ramos: Payment terms: Net 30 is preferred, but finance is open to Net 45 for longer term. Any issues with that?
08:20 Jordan Mills: We can accept Net 45 for enterprise deals with an adjusted pricing tier, but I'd prefer Net 30 in the starter. We'll log it as negotiable.
08:32 Priya Singh: One more DPA item — we want to restrict certain subprocessors and ask for a 30-day notice for changes; otherwise we reserve termination rights.
08:44 Jordan Mills: We typically give 30-day notice and, for critical subprocessors, can build approval gates. We'll propose language.
09:00 Maya Chen: Are there export control considerations? We're working with some EU collaborators and also some controlled data lines.
09:09 Ravi Patel: We do track export controls; data residency plus contractual restrictions can be added. For private, since compute is in your VPC, it's easier to manage; for hosted we have to ensure model artifacts comply. We'll note the export controls clause.
09:28 Maya Chen: Great. Let's go through the immediate deliverables so procurement can finish checklist.
09:34 Jordan Mills: Action items: I'll send an MSA starter and DPA redline friendly doc; Ravi sends the security pack + an infra checklist; pricing spreadsheet with monthly vs committed scenarios to Diego. We'll aim to have those by end of week.
09:49 Priya Singh: We'll prepare our top 5 DPA non-negotiables and circulate. Also want to loop in Redwood legal for a 45-min call — Priya available next Tue/Thu.
10:02 Jordan Mills: Noted. We'll propose Tue 2025-10-14 or Thu 2025-10-16 for legal-to-legal.
10:10 Diego Ramos: Quick question — if we request an escrow for model weights, any precedent?
10:17 Jordan Mills: We have engaged in escrow for some customers; typically that's a separate agreement with associated fees. We'll note it as a potential add-on.
10:26 Liam O'Neal: Regarding incident response: what's the notification SLA for security incidents?
10:31 Ravi Patel: Standard is initial notification within 24 hours for incidents, with a full RCA in 7–30 days depending on severity. We can discuss more strict timelines in the DPA.
10:45 Maya Chen: Good. If we can get the docs ASAP, procurement can package them for legal review.
10:50 Jordan Mills: We'll get them out. Any last blockers from your side?
10:54 Priya Singh: No blockers, just prefer clear redlineable docs.
10:58 Maya Chen: Ok thanks all. Next steps recap and we'll await docs.
11:05 Jordan Mills: Thanks everyone. We'll circulate.
11:10 [meeting ends]

Notes on transcription quality: speaker overlaps sometimes labeled generically; product names occasionally mis-transcribed ("Redwood Privet" instead of Redwood Private; "K-V cash" instead of KV cache).
